title: What's Going on With Bloom Energy Stock? | BE Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc looks at Bloom Energy as data-centre power demand booms, saying he is circling the stock as a potential portfolio addition but that it is not a buy yet. On its latest conference call management said hyperscalers are only the first to embrace onsite power, and more industries will follow; across 15 segments, 35% of facilities are expected to be fully powered onsite by 2035, and the IEA projects global electricity demand rising 40% by 2035 after two flat decades. Bloom is community-friendly because onsite power avoids drawing from the local grid and pushing up local electricity prices, a point of contention where data centres have been opposed. Sales guidance has been raised from over 60% growth to over 120% year on year, and the backlog is growing faster than revenue. The constraint is price: at his roughly $155 DCF target the stock is too expensive, so he keeps watching. Call: BE HOLD, DCF about $155, HOLD reiterated from 31 October. No flip. Bull: electricity demand up 40% by 2035. Bear: buildout delays are the execution risk. No other tickers are called in the video.
